simple.meaning: אִלּוּ (ʼillûw) is a Hebrew word meaning “nay , i.e. (softened) if.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אִלּוּ (H432) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Esther 7:4, with occurrences in Esther, Ecclesiastes.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אִלּוּ (H432) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אִלּוּ (H432) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אִלּוּ (ʼillûw) / H432 is traced through Esther 7:4, Ecclesiastes 6:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for male and female slaves, I would have held my peace, although the adversary could not have compensated for the king’s loss.”
